newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian zinc prices rise on world market gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian zinc prices rise on world market gains.

text.p: Indian zinc prices on Friday rose on the back of gaining world markets, dealers said.
Other base metals moved in a narrow range and settled on a steady note.
Zinc rose by 50 rupees at 7,650 rupees per quintal on limited arrivals, a shortage of ready stock and fresh speculative buying on the back of rising global prices.
Dealers said zinc prices in the world market has risen to a four-year high. In Bombay, they were up by 50 rupees per quintal on Thursday.
Copper was steady at 13,400 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal, respectively on stray physical support. Copper was up by 50 rupees and lead by 25 rupees per quintal on Thursday.
Tin and nickel remained steady at a reduced level in the absence of fresh offerings following a higher trend in the world market. Demand was dull.

Tin was steady at 31,200 rupees and nickel at 37,300 rupees per quintal. Tin was down by 300 rupees and nickel by 200 rupees per quintal on Thursday. Aluminium was unchanged at 7,400 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading.
